independence: Authored from current public documentation and helper interface only; no development query fixtures or prior audit files inspected. Reserved from implementation agents.

scoring.retrieve: Use the unmodified ordinary --search query, retain complete helper JSON, inspect returned section text and advertised section links only.
retrievalMetrics: required facts supported by returned section text
required facts reachable with one explicit linked section read
scoring.factScoring: Each required fact earns 1 only when supported; a qualified/alternative location is acceptable if its actual returned content supports the same fact. Report partial facts rather than all-or-nothing topic matching.
scoring.acceptableLocations: Alternatives are not an exhaustive whitelist. Full-page entries accept any relevant subsection containing the required facts. Multiple sections may jointly cover facts. Do not demand a single canonical answer location.
scoring.limitations: Retrieval coverage is not reader effectiveness. No queries or scoring are revised after seeing candidate retrieval.

questions.query: How should a small expandable details panel handle its own button click and update its controls?
requiredFacts: A View may own local interaction and local state; an Application is not required for a local control.
Use View DOM events with a callback/method; bounded updates to its own controls are appropriate.

questions.query: My title model changes elsewhere, but the View still shows the old title. How do I keep the display in sync?
requiredFacts: Configure the appropriate DataApi for the observable source.
Declare modelEvents (for example change:title or change mapped to render); data changes alone do not render a View.
Model/collection bindings borrow their sources and are released when the View is destroyed.

questions.query: How do I switch an existing editor View to another model without leaving the old model subscribed?
requiredFacts: Call undelegateEntityEvents before changing the model/source.
Assign the replacement source, then call delegateEntityEvents to bind it.
Delegation alone does not release the prior subscription; rebinding does not transfer ownership of the supplied model.

questions.query: I want to sort and temporarily hide rows while keeping the notes typed into each row. Which list operations preserve those rows?
requiredFacts: CollectionView sort/setComparator moves existing rows; filter/setFilter detaches and retains excluded row Views.
Restoring the filter restores retained rows and nodes, but detachment can lose focus.
Full CollectionView render or collection reset rebuilds managed rows; do not use them merely to apply criteria.

questions.query: A row changed from unavailable to available. Its text updated, but it is still hidden by the list filter. What should trigger the filter again?
requiredFacts: A native Model attribute change does not automatically rerun the parent CollectionView filter/sort.
Explicitly call filter() and/or sort() after changing an attribute used by those criteria.
Row modelEvents may rerender the row independently from parent presentation criteria.

questions.query: How can I move a live editor from the sidebar to the main panel without destroying its draft?
requiredFacts: Call the current Region detachView to remove DOM/release ownership while retaining the View.
Show the detached View in the receiving Region; a View must first be detached before another owner adopts it.
The detached View retains its state/listeners; keep a reference and adopt or destroy it later.

questions.query: Updating a status label by rendering my page View removes the editor in its child area. How do I keep the editor alive?
requiredFacts: Rerendering a containing View resets its Regions and destroys child Views.
Update only the changed data/child Region or the local status control, preserving the containing shell and independent editor.
A detached child can be retained deliberately when reconstruction is intended, but retention must be owned explicitly.

questions.query: Where should loading go if the feature must not become ready until it finishes? Will an async onStart delay activation?
requiredFacts: prepareStart is the awaited lifecycle hook and may return a value or Promise.
Its current successful result is supplied to onStart(app, options, result).
Notification hooks such as onStart do not await returned Promises; callers handle start/restart rejection.

questions.query: Reloading the dashboard should keep the current page and unfinished notes visible, including if loading fails. How should its lifecycle work?
requiredFacts: restart repeats preparation while retaining the active root, children, state and subscriptions.
Create/connect the shell only when absent; apply successful prepared results to the changed source or Region in onStart.
A failed active restart rejects but leaves the active feature/UI intact; expose error feedback without stopping it.
stop/start reconstructs UI and is a different lifetime choice.

questions.query: Two reloads finish out of order, and the service ignores abort. How do I keep the older result from replacing the new one?
requiredFacts: A newer restart supersedes pending preparation, aborts its signal, and resolves the earlier call false.
Only the current successful preparation result reaches onStart; apply prepared data there rather than mutating live state in the service.
Pass the signal to dependencies; additional side effects after an await require cancellation checks.
The completed preparation signal is not a lifetime signal for unrelated later operations.

questions.query: One embedded feature needs different rendering and observable state settings. Can I configure it without changing the rest of the app?
requiredFacts: createMarionette returns an isolated family of constructors with configurable providers and Radio.
Configure that runtime or appropriately scoped subclasses before constructing consumers, and use its constructors.
DataApi and StateApi are configured separately; imported adapters alone do not install them.
Provider setters are not a live migration API and do not rebuild existing consumers.

questions.query: My feature survives panel replacement and can stop and start again. Which subscriptions are cleaned up automatically, and which do I need to release?
requiredFacts: Native object destruction removes incoming callbacks and outgoing listenTo subscriptions/bookkeeping; a retained listener needs no per-destroyed-View cleanup handler.
Application stop retains subscriptions to surviving sources; release subscriptions whose useful lifetime ends earlier explicitly.
External listeners/timers/resources need cleanup at their owning lifetime unless their integration guarantees cleanup.
Restart invokes onStart again without onStop; install ongoing effects once per active run and release them on stop.
